title: oxylobium lineare
intro: Oxylobium lineare, commonly known as the New Zealand oak or wharawhara, is a small tree or shrub native to New Zealand. The New Zealand oak has been traditionally used for its medicinal and therapeutic properties, providing health benefits such as wound healing, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects. The therapeutic actions of Oxylobium lineare include its ability to soothe and calm the skin, reducing pain and inflammation, while also exhibiting antioxidant and anti-cancer properties. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal and therapeutic actions.
